subject.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens

question: Should OpenClaw preserve generated macOS LaunchAgent env-file SecretRef credential values during regeneration when current config still references the key?
rationale: The code path is correct and bounded, but preserving credential values across service regeneration is a security and compatibility policy choice that automation should not silently approve.

options.title: Accept bounded preservation
options.body: Land after required checks if maintainers accept retaining file-backed SecretRef credentials only for current managed config keys, with newer state-dir/current-shell values still winning.

options.title: Require exact-head macOS proof
options.body: Ask for the same LaunchAgent regeneration and Telegram getMe proof on the current rebased head before accepting the security boundary.

options.title: Pause for broader env-source policy
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want a broader service-env versus state-dir .env precedence decision before fixing this specific restart/update bug.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded preservation
recommendation.body: Land after required checks if maintainers accept retaining file-backed SecretRef credentials only for current managed config keys, with newer state-dir/current-shell values still winning.

likelyOwner.reason: The history trail ties steipete to the gateway daemon install/config env/auth-profile surfaces and this is a cross-cutting credential-regeneration policy choice.
